assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only solo-leveling:cha-hae-in@original-korean-novel#cha-hae-in-character-reconstruction-model, the active_provisional V1 CHA_HAE_IN_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL at basis_commit, read in full. It reads Chugong's Korean novel omnibus (main story, side stories 1-21 and two postscripts) through whole-novel search and concentrated close reading of the Hunters Guild dungeon, Ahjin application and shadow test, post-Jeju warning, prewar date and reset-world athletic and romantic scenes, with file-level index_split locators. It uses specialist documents 05, 11 and 13 as retrieval maps; those are not curated on this subject and are not used. Manhwa evidence is excluded by the model. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection, and the model's own confidence matrix and A-/B+ rating are treated as method input, not adopted.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The model's six developmental states: Hunters Guild S-rank professional, Jinwoo-curious Ahjin applicant, post-test and post-confession embarrassment, prewar intimacy, reset-world adolescent athlete, and secure reset-world romance and adulthood, each keyed to its anchored scenes (index_split_008-016, 026 and 032). Behavior between anchored scenes and states the model does not name are not assessed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Six invariants (A-F) and a motive structure (privacy, responsibility toward weaker people, competitive integrity, emotional inhibition with initiative) are each tied to named scenes and tested across the pre-reset and reset worlds (II.2, IV). The model is V1 active_provisional, its anchors are file-level and it lists falsification tests still to run (XII), so not B.
Six developmental states with anchored scenes and stated transitions (VII), including the reset as a control that removes hunter identity. Transitions are described, not traced passage by passage.

Speech modes are described with examples (III.2-9), but only a few Korean forms are quoted (당신... 헌터 맞아요?, 편하게, ...네. 그런 것 같아요., 오빠). The roughly 170 candidate turns are expressly not validated stylometry, and sentence endings and honorific levels are left to the V2 plan (XII.3-4).
Ordinary behavior rests on the prewar date and reset-world athletics and Christmas walk (VII.4-6); the model states that sustained everyday friendship and family evidence is sparse (VI.5, XI).

Jinwoo-facing registers are staged across four phases with anchors (VI.1-4); peers, civilians and strong opponents receive shorter, partly behavioral treatment (VI.5-7), and the model warns against generalizing Jinwoo scenes to other relationships (X).

The model draws on narrated physiology and inner reasons: the unstated reason behind 편하게, heartbeat, hiding under covers and relief from being the dependable S-rank (III.5, IV.5, IV.7). These are summarized rather than quoted.

Competitive conflict is well anchored: rejecting the Igris result and demanding Beru, the injured runner's refusal to stop and the renegotiated race condition (II.2 C, IV.3-4). Interpersonal anger is an explicit confidence boundary (IX.4).
A protector ethic is inferred from action (guarding workers, the duty-driven warning; IV.2, III.7); the model rates political and ethical abstraction low-medium and shows no deliberation scene.
Teasing, pouting, jealousy as a question, wagers and the 'if you like me' race manipulation are located in reset-world material concentrated in index_split_032 (III.9, VI.4).

Whole-novel search with concentrated close reading of selected scenes; anchors are file-level, attributed dialogue is not hand-validated, manhwa is excluded and the specialist maps are uncurated here (VIII, XII).

Affirmative limits are located: competitive stubbornness becomes self-endangerment with the ankle injury (IV.4), fear registers physically (II.2 D), and embarrassment produces avoidance and flight (VII.3). The model also corrects the two flattening errors (ice queen, passive love interest).
Behavior is keyed to named states and scenes with split-level locators (VII, VIII), and the model warns against freezing secure Hae-In at the early 편하게 stage.

conditions: Only professional-task, competitive-test or Jinwoo-facing exchanges analogous to anchored scenes, at a named developmental state.
Short utterances in the documented modes; no claims about Korean sentence endings, honorific levels or validated stylometry.
Generated lines are labeled as register approximation, not quotation.
scenario_readiness.note: The described modes support short, register-marked lines in anchored domains; broader or idiomatic Korean dialogue would exceed the quoted evidence.

The decision engine (V) is explicit, but it is a V1 provisional model with file-level anchors, no fidelity validation and evidence concentrated on one partner; novel contexts would rest on unvalidated rules.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One of the model's six named developmental states and its anchored scenes; nothing between or beyond them.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Sung Jinwoo at the matching relationship phase, or hunters and civilians in the anchored professional scenes; the refusal applies equally to other counterparts.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts are not supported.
No family, ordinary-friendship or generalized anger scenes.
No manhwa evidence and no use of the uncurated specialist maps.

scenario_readiness.note: The model itself marks general friendship (medium-low) and family (low-medium) as thin and warns against inventing a casual-friend register.
Values are inferred through protective action; no deliberation is shown, and abstraction is rated low-medium.

conditions: Only with Sung Jinwoo, at an explicitly named phase (curious applicant, post-confession, prewar date, reset-world first encounter or secure romance).
Behavior analogous to the anchored date, confession, warning and reset-world scenes; no other partner.
Escalation beyond the shown range of affection is not supported.
scenario_readiness.note: The Jinwoo relationship is staged from anomaly to secure romance with action-before-speech rules (III.5-9, VI.1-4, IX.5).

conditions: Only hunter field or test situations analogous to the anchored dungeon, Ahjin application and shadow-test scenes.
No guild administration, politics or extended command scenes.
Fear is allowed to register before her judgment decides the action, as the model requires.
scenario_readiness.note: Dungeon vigilance, worker protection, weapon pragmatism and the shadow test are anchored and repeated (II.2 A-C, III.2-4, VII.1-2).

known_limits.statement: The model is V1 active_provisional; its V2 validation (hand-validated dialogue, paragraph-level anchors, competition and risk ledgers, falsification tests) has not been done.
Primary anchors are index_split file locators described as retrieval anchors, not paragraph citations.
Her richest personal evidence is concentrated on Sung Jinwoo and her professional and competitive identity; the model warns against generalizing Jinwoo scenes to unrelated relationships.
The roughly 170 candidate turns are an attribution-adjacent scan, expressly not validated stylometry.
Manhwa visual and body-language evidence is excluded from this subject's model.
There is little evidence for generalized interpersonal anger, family behavior or sustained non-Jinwoo friendship.
The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection, and the specialist documents the model uses as maps are not curated on this subject.
